# The Stars That Wander and the God Who Does Not

## Scripture

*"Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades? Can you loosen Orion's belt? Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons?"* — Job 38:31–32a (NIV)

## Reflection

Step outside on an October evening and you may notice a bright point of light that doesn't stay put. Night after night, it drifts against the backdrop of fixed stars—a wandering planet tracing its slow path across the sky. Ancient observers called these lights "wanderers," and they watched with wonder, never quite knowing where they'd appear next.

We have seasons of wandering too—times when the familiar patterns of life loosen and we're not sure where we're headed. Perhaps a job changes, a friendship shifts, a prayer goes unanswered longer than we expected. In those seasons, it's tempting to believe God has wandered off as well.

But Job 38 reminds us who holds the constellations. God asks Job if he can bind the Pleiades or guide Orion—questions meant not to shame but to comfort. The One who keeps wandering planets on their course also keeps us. Our seasons of uncertainty are not outside His sight; they are held within His steady hand.

Even the planets never truly wander *away*—they follow an orbit set by their Maker. So it is with us. When life feels unmoored, we are still held in the gravity of a faithful God who knows exactly where we are and where we're going.

## Prayer

Lord of the wandering stars, thank You that no season of uncertainty escapes Your notice. When life feels directionless, remind us that You hold our path as surely as You hold the constellations. Steady our hearts in Your faithfulness. Amen.
